raw_text:
name: dotnet-csharp-source-generators

Guidance for creating and consuming Roslyn source generators: `IIncrementalGenerator`, syntax providers, semantic analysis, deterministic emission, diagnostics, testing with `CSharpGeneratorDriver`, built-in generators (`[GeneratedRegex]`, `[LoggerMessage]`, System.Text.Json `[JsonSerializable]`), and NuGet packaging.

Related skills: [skill:dotnet-roslyn-analyzers] for analyzers/code fixes; [skill:dotnet-csharp-modern-patterns] for modern C# and partial properties; [skill:dotnet-csharp-coding-standards] for naming.

Generators ship as analyzers targeting `netstandard2.0`.

```xml
<TargetFramework>netstandard2.0</TargetFramework>
<EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>true</EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>
<IsRoslynComponent>true</IsRoslynComponent>
<LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers" Version="3.3.4" PrivateAssets="all" />
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="4.12.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
```

**Always target `netstandard2.0`.** Generators load into the compiler process, which requires this TFM for compatibility. Use `LangVersion>latest` to write modern C# in the generator itself.

Always use `IIncrementalGenerator` over the legacy `ISourceGenerator`. Incremental generators are cache-aware and only re-run when inputs change, making them significantly faster in IDE scenarios.

Pipeline: use `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` or `CreateSyntaxProvider` with a tight predicate; transform to simple data (strings/records); group and emit via `RegisterSourceOutput`. Never pass `ISymbol` or `SyntaxNode` through the pipeline (they hold the compilation alive and break caching). Use `record struct` or implement `IEquatable<T>` for custom pipeline values. Emit deterministic output (`// <auto-generated/>`, `#nullable enable`); use fully qualified names and collision-safe hint names.

Example scope: top-level, non-generic classes. A production generator should also handle generic type parameters and nested types. Report a diagnostic for unsupported shapes rather than emitting invalid code.

Report errors and warnings through `SourceProductionContext` rather than throwing exceptions. Capture `Location` from syntax for location-specific diagnostics; `Location` is not value-equatable, so including it in your pipeline record breaks incremental caching. Exclude it from equality or report diagnostics before projecting to value types.

Use `RegisterPostInitializationOutput` for marker attributes/helper types independent of user code. Use `{TypeName}.{Feature}.g.cs`; `.g.cs` signals generated code. Prefer raw string literals for templates.

Testing: use `CSharpGeneratorDriver` to run generators in-memory and verify output; assert no error diagnostics and inspect generated trees. For snapshot tests, use [Verify.SourceGenerators](https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.SourceGenerators).

Built-in generators:
- `[GeneratedRegex]`: method must be `static partial` returning `Regex`, inside a `partial class` or `partial struct`. Replaces `new Regex(...)` with zero runtime allocation; AOT-compatible. Supports all `RegexOptions` except `RegexOptions.Compiled` (ignored).
- `[LoggerMessage]`: methods must be `static partial` in a `partial class`. `{Placeholder}` parameters are structured data; `Exception` is logged automatically (do not include in message template). Event IDs are auto-assigned; specify explicit IDs for stable telemetry.
- System.Text.Json: register serialized types with `[JsonSerializable]`; use `TypeInfoResolverChain` (net8.0+) to combine contexts. Required for Native AOT because reflection-based serialization is trimmed. Supports polymorphism with `[JsonDerivedType]`.

NuGet: place generator assembly under `analyzers/dotnet/cs/`; include `_._` if no runtime dependency. Example packaging:
```xml
<IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>
<DevelopmentDependency>true</DevelopmentDependency>
<None Include="$(OutputPath)\$(AssemblyName).dll"
      PackagePath="analyzers/dotnet/cs" />
```
Debug workflow: `System.Diagnostics.Debugger.Launch()` if `!System.Diagnostics.Debugger.IsAttached`. To inspect files, set `<EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>true</EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>` and `<CompilerGeneratedFilesOutputPath>Generated</CompilerGeneratedFilesOutputPath>` in the consuming project. Add `Generated/` to `.gitignore`.

References:
- [Source Generator Cookbook](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.cookbook.md)
- [Incremental Generators](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md)
- [GeneratedRegex source generator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/regular-expression-source-generators)
- [Compile-time logging source generation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/extensions/logger-message-generator)
- [System.Text.Json source generation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/source-generation)
- [.NET Framework Design Guidelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/)
